thread:
liam: Quick check — proto-first gRPC vs JSON/REST for the new internal routing surface? Thinking about quotas, console UX, and rollout signals.
jen: Short answer: proto gives us stronger contracts + easier attribution for quotas. JSON wins for browser SDKs and discoverability.
arik: Can we do dual-stack (gRPC inside, JSON at edge)? worried about latency + cost + extra ops.
dan: For routing policies we really want typed fields. If route keys are part of the payload, proto avoids fragile parsing in proxies.
jen: Yup. Also Console examples are way cleaner with JSON samples. Search/samples + copy-paste for users matter for PLG.
sasha: FWIW we had complaints last quarter about browser teams struggling with gRPC-web setup.
liam: Important nuance: telemetry. With proto we can attach explicit route tags in the envelope and get precise per-route metrics. With JSON we rely on heuristics or parsing.
arik: Another angle — rollout UX. Canarying model variants per route needs consistent request keys to evaluate quality regressions. Proto -> stable key shapes.
dan: Implementation option: central translator that accepts JSON, converts to proto for internal services. Pros: keeps internal strong typing. Cons: extra CPU and edge complexity.
liam: Edge translator also complicates rate limiting. Do we enforce quotas at translator level (early) or let backends enforce (consistent with typed fields)?
jen: I prefer quota enforcement at edge to give early feedback. But then edge needs to understand tenant+route semantics — duplicating logic.
dan: Could send signed route-claims header from edge to backend after validation. That reduces backends' parsing burden.
sasha: Signing adds cryptography + key rotation concerns. Also visibility in Console needs that header to be surfaced.
liam: Example mapping idea (pseudo):
```http
POST /v1/generate
Accept: application/json
X-Tenant: acct_123
Body: {"route": "text-complete", "input": "foo"}
# Edge -> translate -> internal gRPC: GenerateRequest{ tenant_id: "acct_123", route_key: "text-complete", prompt: "foo" }
```
jen: That looks fine. But streaming responses are a pain with transliteration — gRPC streaming vs chunked JSON.
arik: Streaming aside, main tradeoffs: telemetry fidelity, quota enforcement point, browser ergonomics, ops complexity, failure modes.
liam: Failure modes: if edge translator is down we need fallback to a lightweight JSON passthrough or direct gRPC (if client supports it). Fallback must be graceful.
dan: Suggestion: support "best-effort" dual-mode for 6 months: JSON fronting + internal proto. Build a small shim that emits route-claims header and trace IDs. Run canary on a subset of tenants.
jen: We should evaluate cost delta — extra CPU for translator + added latency. I'll run a quick cost estimate.
sasha: Also add Console work: show raw route-claim header in request inspector and add a toggle to view proto fields translated.
liam: Action items:
- jen: cost estimate for translator (eta Wed)
- arik: POC translator repo + latency bench (eta Fri)
- dan: design header signing + rotation doc (eta next Tue)
- sasha: Console mockups for showing translated payloads (eta next Mon)
everyone: react with :thumbsup: if you agree to dual-mode POC.
